bib.title: Transformers are RNNs: Fast Autoregressive Transformers with Linear Attention
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 37th International Conference on Machine Learning (ICML), PMLR 119, 2020

question: Can self-attention be computed in time and memory linear in sequence length, and make autoregressive transformer inference fast, without losing quality?
hypothesis: Replacing softmax with a kernel feature-map dot product and using associativity gives linear complexity and an RNN form with similar quality to softmax attention.
contributions: Linear transformer: kernel feature-map formulation of attention with O(N) time and memory
Causal masking with linear complexity and constant memory, with gradients as cumulative sums
Showing any causal transformer layer can be written as an RNN, giving much faster autoregressive inference

method.summary: Attention is rewritten as phi(Q)(phi(K)^T V) with phi(x)=elu(x)+1. With causal masking the layer becomes a recurrence with state S_i and normaliser Z_i. Compared with softmax and Reformer on a synthetic copy task, MNIST and CIFAR-10 image generation, and WSJ speech recognition.
method.task: efficient attention; copy task, autoregressive image generation, CTC speech recognition

datasets.name: Synthetic copy task
datasets.size: sequences of max length 128, 10 symbols plus separator

models.name: Linear transformer (phi=elu+1)
models.hidden: embedding 256, 32 per head, FFN 4x embedding (image tasks)

other.output: mixture of 10 logistics for images (Salimans et al. 2017)
other.cuda: constant-memory gradient in approx. 200 lines of CUDA

models.name: Reformer (lsh-1, lsh-4, lsh-8)
models.architecture: PyTorch reimplementation of published code, no reversible layers

other.buckets: 64; MNIST 27 chunks of 29 elements; CIFAR-10 83 chunks of 37 elements

models.name: Stateful-softmax
models.architecture: softmax transformer caching keys and values (Appendix C.1)

training.objective: cross-entropy (copy); mixture of 10 logistics likelihood, bits/dim (images); CTC loss (WSJ)
training.lr: copy 1e-3 then 1e-4 after 3000 updates; MNIST 1e-4; WSJ transformers 1e-4 initial, Bi-LSTM 1e-3
training.lr_schedule: WSJ: divided by 2 (transformers) or reduced (LSTM) when validation error stops decreasing
training.epochs: MNIST 250; CIFAR-10 fixed 7 days; WSJ to convergence
training.seq_len: copy 128; MNIST 784 pixels; CIFAR-10 almost 4x MNIST (inferred: not stated numerically)
training.hardware: CIFAR-10: NVidia P40 24GB; benchmark: GTX 1080 Ti 11GB
training.compute: CIFAR-10: 7 days per model on a single GPU

other.CIFAR-10 sequence length: inferred: 'almost 4 times larger' than 784; not stated numerically

other.benchmark: N in 2^9..2^16, batch size scaled inversely with length, peak GPU memory and time per sample; softmax max length 4,096, lsh-4/8 16,384 on 11GB

metrics.name: bits/dim
metrics.definition: test negative log-likelihood per pixel dimension

eval.protocol: single runs; no seeds or significance tests stated

evidence.quote: the full transformer can only be used with a batch size of 1 in the largest GPU that is available to us

results.claim: Linear transformer generates CIFAR-10 images 4,462x faster than softmax (recompute baseline).
results.setup: CIFAR-10 autoregressive, 16 layers, 7 days single GPU, batch 1 for softmax
results.note: Table prints 4,462x, text prints 4,460 and 'more than 4,000x'; abstract says up to 4000x

results.claim: Linear reaches 3.40 bits/dim vs softmax 3.47 on CIFAR-10 under equal 7-day budget.
results.table: Table 2, rows Linear (ours) and Softmax, column Bits/dim

results.claim: Against stateful-softmax (cached keys/values), linear is more than 50x faster on CIFAR-10.
results.quote: our forumlation is more than 50× faster for CIFAR-10
results.note: Table 4b: 17.85 vs 0.32 is 55.8x; text says more than 50x

results.claim: MNIST: linear 0.644 bits/dim vs softmax 0.621 at 142.8 vs 0.45 images/sec.
results.quote: more than 300 times higher throughput in image generation

results.claim: WSJ speech: softmax best PER, linear 8.08 beats Bi-LSTM 10.94 and LSH-4 9.33.
results.quote:
Note that the softmax transformer, achieves
lower phone error rate in comparison to all baselines
results.table: Table 3, row Linear (ours), column Validation PER

results.claim: Linear is more than 3x faster per epoch than softmax on WSJ.
results.quote:
linear transformer
is more than 3× faster per epoch

results.claim: On the copy task linear reaches the same loss as softmax and lower than lsh-4.
results.setup: 4 layers, 8 heads, batch 64, RAdam, seq length 128
results.quote: In particular, it reaches the same loss as softmax.

results.claim: Softmax max sequence length is 4,096 on an 11GB GTX 1080 Ti; lsh-4/8 reach 16,384.
results.quote:
This
results in a maximum sequence length of 4,096 elements
for softmax and 16,384 for lsh-4 and lsh-8.

results.claim: Single-image latency at batch 1 on GPU, CIFAR-10: linear 61.3 s vs softmax 300.1 s.
results.note: Text says almost 6.6x faster than softmax for CIFAR-10 image latency, table shows 4.9x on GPU (300.1 vs 61.3) and 191.8x on CPU

limits: Softmax transformer remains better on WSJ speech recognition (PER 5.12 vs 8.08)
Experiments are small (MNIST, CIFAR-10, WSJ, copy task); no language modelling or pretrained models
Feature map elu+1 only; authors suggest random Fourier features to reuse softmax-pretrained models as future work
Speedups are measured against a softmax baseline without key/value caching; stateful-softmax closes much of the gap (Appendix C)
Single runs, no seeds or variance reported
At batch 1 the speedup is much smaller (about 4.9x on GPU) because the sequence loop dominates

terms.definition: transformer whose attention uses a feature-map dot product phi(Q)phi(K)^T, computed with associativity in O(N)

lineage.work: Attention is all you need (Vaswani et al.)

lineage.note: LSH attention, O(N log N); also copy task source

lineage.work: Generating long sequences with sparse transformers (Child et al.)
Adaptive sampled softmax with kernel based sampling (Blanc & Rendle)

figures.caption: Comparison of the computational requirements for a forward/backward pass for Reformer (lsh-X), softmax attention and linear attention.
figures.why: Shows quadratic vs linear scaling of time and memory with length

figures.caption: We train autoregressive transformers for 1 week on a single GPU to generate CIFAR-10 images.

code.snippet: s_i = s_{i-1} + phi(x_i W_K)(x_i W_V)^T; z_i = z_{i-1} + phi(x_i W_K); y_i = f_l(phi(x_i W_Q)^T s_i / phi(x_i W_Q)^T z_i + x_i)
